name: Carlos G. Muñiz
background: Born in Chicago in 1969; University of Virginia B.A. (1991) and Yale Law School J.D. (1997); clerked for Judges Thomas Flannery (D.D.C.) and José Cabranes (2d Cir.). Had never been a judge before his appointment: he was deputy general counsel to Gov. Jeb Bush, general counsel of the Department of Financial Services, deputy chief of staff to House Speaker Marco Rubio, deputy attorney general and chief of staff to Attorney General Pam Bondi (2011–2014), and Senate-confirmed general counsel of the U.S. Department of Education under Betsy DeVos (2018–2019). Federalist Society member. Served as chief justice July 2022–June 30, 2026; voters retained him in 2020 with 65.75% yes.
notableOpinions: Joined the 6-1 majority in Planned Parenthood v. State (April 2024) holding the state constitution's privacy clause does not protect abortion, overruling In re T.W. (1989) and allowing the 6-week ban to take effect; at oral argument he questioned whether 'natural person' excludes the unborn. As chief justice he wrote the 2025 majority in Black Voters Matter v. Byrd upholding the DeSantis congressional map that eliminated a majority-Black North Florida district (Justice Labarga dissented). Also joined 2020 rulings loosening the standard for overruling precedent and adopting the federal summary-judgment standard, and criticized the Public Service Commission as a 'black box' in a 2023–24 FPL rate case.
barPoll: No 2026 poll exists; The Florida Bar discontinued its merit-retention poll in 2023. In the last poll (2020) 71% of responding lawyers recommended retention overall, the lowest of any jurist polled that year among those with 'considerable knowledge' (63%).
positions: Yes: Pinellas County Republican Party slate and Republican Party of Florida Pinellas guide; Florida Family Action's 2026 Judicial Guide marks 'YES' for Muñiz. No: Miami Herald editorial board (per Florida Trib, Oct 26, 2026); Creative Loafing Tampa (op-ed by editor Ray Roa, Oct 13, 2026, and its voting guide); South Florida Sun Sentinel editorial board lists 'Carlos Muñiz (Retention): No' per WLRN's Oct 23, 2026 guide, although Florida Trib (Oct 26) reported the Sun Sentinel said he 'deserves retention' — the two reports conflict and could not be reconciled. No Tampa Bay Times recommendation found as of Oct 27, 2026; no Equality Florida or organized PAC campaign found. Voter Action Pinellas (Democratic-aligned) flags his DeSantis appointment, redistricting vote and Federalist Society ties without a formal recommendation. No Florida Supreme Court justice has ever lost a retention vote.
lgbtqNote: None identified. No LGBTQ+-specific opinion or statement was found; progressive critics focus on his abortion and redistricting rulings and Federalist Society affiliation.

name: Drew Atkinson
background: J. Andrew 'Drew' Atkinson, 52–53, born in Gainesville and raised in Bradenton; U.S. Army Ranger sergeant (1st Bn., 75th Ranger Regiment, 1997–2001); FSU B.A. (1996), Nova Southeastern J.D. with honors (2005). Worked in the Attorney General's criminal appeals division and as deputy solicitor general, clerked for Judge Melanie May (4th DCA), was assistant general counsel to Gov. Scott, practiced at Broad and Cassel, and served as general counsel of the Florida Departments of State and Management Services before his 2018 appointment. Retained in 2020 with about 70.9% yes. Voter Action Pinellas notes a Federalist Society affiliation.
notableOpinions: Wrote for a three-judge panel in the Howell Donaldson III (Seminole Heights murders) case, reversing a Tampa trial court's limits on the evidence a jury could hear across four separate trials; Donaldson later pleaded guilty and received four consecutive life sentences (Tampa Bay Times, Oct 2026). No other widely reported opinions found. Serves on the Supreme Court's Standard Jury Instructions (Criminal) committee and the DCA Performance and Accountability commission. No Judicial Qualifications Commission proceedings reported.
barPoll: No 2026 poll (Bar poll discontinued 2023). 2020 Florida Bar poll: 76% recommended retention.
positions: Yes: Pinellas County Republican Party slate and Republican Party of Florida Pinellas guide. No: Creative Loafing Tampa 2026 voting guide (no reasoning published). Florida Family Action's guide lists him without a visible yes/no mark in the text layer. No Tampa Bay Times, Equality Florida, or organized campaign found; Voter Action Pinellas flags his Scott appointment and Federalist Society ties without a recommendation.

name: Morris Silberman
background: Age 69; Tulane B.A. (philosophy and political science), University of Florida J.D. (1982). Clerked for 2nd DCA Judge Herboth Ryder, practiced business litigation and appeals in Sarasota and Clearwater, and formed his own Clearwater firm in 1988. Longest-serving of the four; chief judge 2011–2013; past chair of the Judicial Qualifications Commission (member 2003–2012); Florida Bar Board of Governors 1996–2000; president of the Council of Chief Judges of the State Courts of Appeal (2021–22); National Center for State Courts board; American Law Institute member. Married to fellow 2nd DCA Judge Nelly Khouzam. Retained in 2020 with 71.06% yes (and in prior cycles since 2002).
notableOpinions: No individually prominent opinions surfaced in 2026 coverage; he is regarded as an institutional, appellate-practice-oriented judge with extensive court-administration service. No Judicial Qualifications Commission proceedings reported.
barPoll: No 2026 poll (Bar poll discontinued 2023). 2020 Florida Bar poll: 90% recommended retention, highest of the four 2nd DCA judges on the 2026 ballot.
positions: Yes: Pinellas County Republican Party slate and Republican Party of Florida Pinellas guide; Creative Loafing Tampa 2026 voting guide. No organized 'No' campaign, Tampa Bay Times recommendation, or Equality Florida position found. Voter Action Pinellas notes only his appointment by Gov. Bush.

name: Daniel H. Sleet
appointedBy: Gov. Rick Scott (December 2012); earlier appointed to the 13th Judicial Circuit by Gov. Jeb Bush (2005)
background: Age 65; Furman B.A. in history (1984), Cumberland School of Law J.D. (1987). Hillsborough assistant state attorney 1987–1991 handling serious felonies, then personal-injury defense partner at Barr, Murman & Tonelli in Tampa (1991–2005); Supreme Court-certified mediator. Hillsborough circuit judge 2005–2012 (re-elected unopposed 2008). Chief judge of the 2nd DCA 2023–July 2025; chairs the court's Legislative Committee; American Board of Trial Advocates member and adjunct trial-advocacy professor at University of Tampa since 2016. Retained in 2020 with 70.96% yes.
notableOpinions: No individually prominent opinions surfaced in 2026 coverage. A 2020 personal blog claimed he 'voted in favor of a change that strengthened the Stand Your Ground law' later found unconstitutional; that claim is unsourced and could not be verified. No Judicial Qualifications Commission proceedings reported.
barPoll: No 2026 poll (Bar poll discontinued 2023). 2020 Florida Bar poll: 85% recommended retention.
positions: Yes: Pinellas County Republican Party slate and Republican Party of Florida Pinellas guide; Creative Loafing Tampa 2026 voting guide. No organized 'No' campaign, Tampa Bay Times recommendation, or Equality Florida position found. Voter Action Pinellas notes only his appointment by Gov. Scott.

name: Andrea Teves Smith
appointedBy: Gov. Rick Scott (2019); earlier appointed to the 10th Judicial Circuit by Gov. Scott (2013)
background: Age 57; University of Florida B.S. in business administration, Stetson J.D. Spent 19 years at a Lakeland firm handling commercial litigation and appeals, becoming a shareholder with an AV Preeminent rating. Polk County circuit judge 2013–2019 (retained by election 2014), serving as administrative judge of the civil division. Reported to be the first Asian Pacific American appellate judge in Florida. Retained to the 2nd DCA in 2020 with 75.0% yes.
notableOpinions: No individually prominent opinions surfaced in 2026 coverage; a 2020 guide said she had not served long enough to leave a track record, and no major reported rulings since were found. No Judicial Qualifications Commission proceedings reported.
barPoll: No 2026 poll (Bar poll discontinued 2023). 2020 Florida Bar poll: 82% recommended retention.
positions: Yes: Pinellas County Republican Party slate and Republican Party of Florida Pinellas guide. No: Creative Loafing Tampa 2026 voting guide (no reasoning published). No Tampa Bay Times recommendation, Equality Florida position, or organized campaign found. Voter Action Pinellas notes only her appointment by Gov. Scott.
